17.2.1 Preparation of Grignard Reagents

Grignard reagents are prepared in the laboratory by the action of alkyl or aryl halides on freshly prepared magnesium metal in anhydrous or dry ether i.e. diethyl ether or tetrahydrofuran.

It is an example of heterogeneous reaction, in which solid magnesium react with alkyl halide in ether. Grignard reagent cannot be isolated, therefore, its ethereal solution is directly used in the synthetic reactions.

The ease of formation of Grignard reagent depends upon the nature of both alkyl and aryl group and the nature of halogen. Increasing size of the alkyl group makes the formation of Grignard reagent difficult. For the same alkyl group, the ease of formation increases down the group i.e. from fluorine to iodine. Alkyl magnesium fluorides and chloride are not obtained with good yield. Alkyl iodides are the most reactive but still bromides are used more commonly for preparation of Grignard reagent because bromides are less expensive and less toxic than iodides.

Diethyl ether used in the preparation of Grignard reagent plays two important roles. At one hand, it provides a medium for the reaction, at the other hand, it dissolves the Grignard reagent by the process of solvation. Crystalline Grignard reagent obtained by cooling ethereal solution of Grignard reagent, have been found to be dietherate in which magnesium has been coordinated with two molecules of ethers, in addition to having two covalent bonds. The four groups are arranged tetrahedrally around magnesium.

17.2.2 Reactivity of Grignard Reagents

The carbon magnesium bond of Grignard reagent is polar in nature. This is due to higher electronegativity of carbon than magnesium. So the electronic density is lying close to carbon than magnesium. As a result of this electronegativity difference, the carbon atom has a partial negative while magnesium has a partial positive charge. R⁻ᵟ–Mg⁺ᵟX

The alkyl group being an electron rich centre, acts as carbanion or nucleophile. It would attack polarized molecules at the point of low electronic density. Therefore, the characteristic reactions of Grignard reagents are nucleophilic substitution and nucleophilic addition reactions.

گرینیارڈ عامل کی تیاری میں استعمال ہونے والا ڈائی ایتھائل ایتھر دو اہم کردار ادا کرتا ہے۔ ایک طرف یہ تعامل کے لیے واسطہ فراہم کرتا ہے، دوسری طرف یہ سولویشن کے عمل سے گرینیارڈ عامل کو حل کرتا ہے۔ گرینیارڈ عامل کے ایتھری محلول کو ٹھنڈا کر کے حاصل ہونے والا قلمی گرینیارڈ عامل ڈائی ایتھریٹ پایا گیا ہے جس میں میگنیشیم دو شریک گرفتی بندوں کے علاوہ ایتھر کے دو سالمات سے کوآرڈینیٹ ہوتی ہے۔ یہ چار گروپ میگنیشیم کے گرد چہار سطحی ترتیب میں ہوتے ہیں۔

17.2 Organometallic Compounds (Grignard Reagents)

All those organic compounds which contain at least one carbon–metal bond in their structures are known as organometallic compounds. You are already familiar with at least one organometallic compound, sodium acetylide (Na⁺⁻C ≡ CH), (Section 16.7.7) which has an ionic bond between carbon and sodium. Organometallic compounds are generally represented by the formula: R–M or Ar–M

Where, M = Mg, Li, Hg, Cu, Pb, Zn etc. and R- and Ar- represent any alkyl or aryl groups respectively. They are named simply by adding the name of the metal to the organic group bonded directly to the metal. Examples;

Alkyl or aryl magnesium halides (organomagnesium compounds) are commonly known as Grignard reagents. They were discovered, prepared and studied by victor Grignard, therefore, they were named after him as Grignard reagents. They are highly reactive organic compounds, and are used in the synthesis of a large number of organic compounds. Due to this great achievement Grignard was awarded with Nobel Prize in 1912. The general formula of Grignard reagents is, R–MgX where R represent Alkyl group (can also be vinylic or aryl group) and X represent halogen atom. Examples are;

17.2.1 Preparation of Grignard Reagents

Grignard reagents are prepared in the laboratory by the action of alkyl or aryl halides on freshly prepared magnesium metal in anhydrous or dry ether i.e. diethyl ether or tetrahydrofuran.

It is an example of heterogeneous reaction, in which solid magnesium react with alkyl halide in ether. Grignard reagent cannot be isolated, therefore, its ethereal solution is directly used in the synthetic reactions.

The ease of formation of Grignard reagent depends upon the nature of both alkyl and aryl group and the nature of halogen. Increasing size of the alkyl group makes the formation of Grignard reagent difficult. For the same alkyl group, the ease of formation increases down the group i.e. from fluorine to iodine. Alkyl magnesium fluorides and chloride are not obtained with good yield. Alkyl iodides are the most reactive but still bromides are used more commonly for preparation of Grignard reagent because bromides are less expensive and less toxic than iodides.

Diethyl ether used in the preparation of Grignard reagent plays two important roles. At one hand, it provides a medium for the reaction, at the other hand, it dissolves the Grignard reagent by the process of solvation. Crystalline Grignard reagent obtained by cooling ethereal solution of Grignard reagent, have been found to be dietherate in which magnesium has been coordinated with two molecules of ethers, in addition to having two covalent bonds. The four groups are arranged tetrahedrally around magnesium.

Figure 17.4 Tetrahedral dietherate of Grignard reagent.

17.2.2 Reactivity of Grignard Reagents

The carbon magnesium bond of Grignard reagent is polar in nature. This is due to higher electronegativity of carbon than magnesium. So the electronic density is lying close to carbon than magnesium. As a result of this electronegativity difference, the carbon atom has a partial negative while magnesium has a partial positive charge. R⁻ᵟ–Mg⁺ᵟX

The alkyl group being an electron rich centre, acts as carbanion or nucleophile. It would attack polarized molecules at the point of low electronic density. Therefore, the characteristic reactions of Grignard reagents are nucleophilic substitution and nucleophilic addition reactions.

17.2.3 Reactions of Grignard Reagents

Grignard reagents are highly reactive compounds. Therefore, they react with many organic and inorganic compounds to produce a large number of valuable products. Some of these reactions are as follows.
